10	/-!
11	# FGA representability of the Picard scheme
12	
13	This file states the FGA representability of the relative Picard functor of a
14	smooth proper geometrically integral curve `C/k`, following Kleiman, "The
15	Picard scheme", §2 and §4 (cf. FGA Explained Ch. 9; arXiv:math/0504020).
16	
17	The relative Picard functor is
18	
19	```
20	picSharp C := PicSharp.relPresheaf C ⋙ forget AddCommGrpCat
21	```
22	
23	the set-valued shadow of the `H_T`-coset carrier
24	`T ↦ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)` of `Picard/RelPicFunctor.lean` (Kleiman §2
25	Def. `df:Pfs`; blueprint `def:rel_pic_sharp`). A `RepresentableBy` witness
26	against it is a natural bijection
27	`(T ⟶ Pic_{C/k}) ≃ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)`, which is what the downstream
28	tangent-space computation (`AJC.pic0av`, `Pic0.tangentSpaceIso`) attaches to.
29	
30	## The étale-sheafification route: Kleiman §2 Thm 2.5
31	
32	Kleiman §4 represents the **étale-sheafified** functor `Pic_{(C/k)ét}`.
33	Mathlib at the pinned revision has no étale Grothendieck topology on
34	schemes, so instead of sheafifying we use Kleiman §2 **Thm 2.5**: when
35	`f : X → S` has a **section** and `O_S = f_* O_X` holds universally (true
36	for our proper geometrically integral `C/k`), the comparison maps
37	
38	```
39	Pic_{X/S}(T) → Pic_{(X/S)ét}(T) → Pic_{(X/S)fppf}(T)
40	```
41	
42	are all **bijective**. Hence, under a `k`-rational-point hypothesis
43	(`HasRationalPoint C` below), the *plain* relative functor `picSharp C` is
44	itself representable, and the FGA statement can be made against it directly
45	— no étale topology needed. Without a section the plain functor is not
46	representable in general (it need not even be a Zariski sheaf), which is why
47	representability is asserted only **conditionally on `[HasRationalPoint C]`**:
48	an unconditional statement would be false. For the same reason `picSharp` may
49	not be wired to the *absolute* functor `PicSharp.presheaf`.
50	
51	## Main results
52	
53	* `picSharp` — the relative Picard functor `Pic^♯_{C/k}`.
54	* `divFunctor` — the relative-divisor functor `Scheme.DivFunctor C.hom` of
55	  `Picard/DivFunctorDef.lean` (Kleiman §3 Def. `df:div`, invertible-kernel
56	  quotient encoding).
57	* `PicScheme`, `representable`, `instPicSharpRepresentable` — the representing
58	  scheme and the natural bijection
59	  `(T ⟶ Pic_{C/k}) ≃ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)` it induces.
60	* `instPicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType`, `isSeparated` — `Pic_{C/k}` is locally
61	  of finite type and separated over `k` (Kleiman §4 Thm `th:main`(1): it is a
62	  disjoint union of open quasi-projective `k`-subschemes).
63	* `groupSchemeStructure` — `Pic_{C/k}` is a commutative `k`-group scheme, by
64	  Yoneda transport (`CommGrpObj.ofRepresentableBy`) of the abelian-group
65	  structure of `PicSharp.relPresheaf`.
66	* `abelMapWitness`, `abelMap`, `abelMap_app_mk` — the Abel map
67	  `Div_{C/k} ⟶ Pic^♯_{C/k}`, `[D] ↦ [O(D)] = -[ker q]` (Kleiman §3
68	  Def. `dfn:Abel`), assembled as `abelKernelNatTrans C ≫ picNeg C`.
69	* `smoothProperQuotient` — the Altman–Kleiman quotient lemma (Kleiman §4
70	  Lem. `lm:qt`), relative to the use-site hypothesis class
71	  `HasSmoothProperQuotient`.
72	
73	## Remaining obligations
74	
75	One statement in this file is still `sorry`: `instHasPicScheme`, the existence
76	of a scheme that represents `picSharp C` and is separated and locally of
77	finite type over `k`, given a rational point. Mathematically this is Kleiman
78	§4 Thm `th:main`(1) together with Cor `cor:algsch`, transported through §2
79	Thm 2.5. Everything else here — in particular representability of the chosen
80	scheme, its local finiteness, its separatedness, and its group-scheme
81	structure — is derived from that one existence statement.
82	
83	`smoothProperQuotient` is stated against an explicit hypothesis class rather
84	than proved outright, because the hypothesis list expressible here is weaker
85	than Kleiman §4 Lem. `lm:qt`: it omits quasi-projectivity of the representing
86	scheme `Y`, for which Mathlib has no vocabulary at the pinned revision.
87	Without that hypothesis the statement is false — a Hironaka-type free
88	`ℤ/2`-action on a smooth proper non-projective 3-fold gives a smooth proper
89	equivalence relation whose quotient étale sheaf is an algebraic space that is
90	not a scheme. The class must therefore be supplied at the use site, where
91	quasi-projectivity of the Abel-map slice is available.
92

97	(`th:comp` comparison under a section), §3 Def `dfn:Abel` + Thm `th:repDiv`,
98	§4 Thm `th:main` + Cor `cor:algsch` + Lem `lm:qt`.
99	-/

267	/-! ## §2. The Abel map — line-bundle / Quot correspondence
268	
269	The bridge from line bundles on `C ×_k T` to the Quot scheme is the **Abel
270	map**: a relative effective divisor `D ⊆ C ×_k T` over `T` determines a
271	`T`-point of `Div_{C/k}`, and the dual ideal sheaf
272	`O_{C ×_k T}(D) := I_D⁻¹` represents a class in `Pic^♯_{C/k}(T)`.
273	
274	Blueprint reference: `lem:line_bundle_quot_correspondence` (Kleiman §3
275	Def. `dfn:Abel` + Thm. `th:repDiv`). -/
276	
277	/-! ### The Abel map
278	
279	The class `HasAbelMap` carries the map itself (a data field `abel`), so that
280	`abelMap` has the defining property `abelMap_app_mk` below; the instance
281	supplies the explicit natural transformation `abelMapWitness C`.
282	
283	Construction of `abelMapWitness C : Div_{C/k} ⟶ Pic^♯_{C/k}`, `[D] ↦ [O(D)]`:
284	a relative effective divisor family `⟨F, q⟩` on `C ×_k T` has invertible ideal
285	`I_D = ker q`; the Abel map sends its class to
286	`[O(D)] = [I_D⁻¹] = -[I_D]`, the additive inverse (in the group-valued target
287	`Pic^♯_{C/k}(T)`) of the class of the ideal sheaf.  It is assembled as the
288	composite `abelKernelNatTrans C ≫ picNeg C`, where `abelKernelNatTrans` is the
289	substantive `[D] ↦ [I_D]` transformation and `picNeg` is the (natural)
290	negation on the group-valued functor.
291	
292	Naturality of `abelKernelNatTrans` is the mathematical heart: for a test map
293	`g : T' ⟶ T` the base-change square is cartesian (`quotBaseSquare`), and the
294	**kernel–pullback comparison** `g_C^*(ker q) ⟶ ker(g_C^* q)` is an isomorphism
295	under the divisor conditions (`Modules.isIso_pullbackKernelComparison`, whose
296	side hypotheses — epi `q`, quasi-coherent source, finitely-presented `F`,
297	`T`-flat `F`, invertible kernel — are exactly the fields of `DivFamily`), so
298	`ker` commutes with base change and the class `[ker q]` is natural.  Negation
299	is natural because `Pic^♯`'s pullback maps are group homomorphisms.
300

453	/-! ## §3. The smooth-proper quotient lemma — Altman–Kleiman descent
454	
455	The structural lemma underlying Step 4 of Kleiman §4 Thm. `th:main`: given a
456	surjection `α : Z ⟶ P` of étale sheaves with `R := Z ×_P Z` representable,
457	`Z` representable **by a quasi-projective scheme**, and the first projection
458	`R ⟶ Z` smooth and proper, the quotient `P` is representable.
459	
460	The hypothesis list expressible here is strictly weaker than Kleiman §4 Lem
461	`lm:qt`: it lacks **quasi-projectivity of `Y`**, for which Mathlib has no
462	vocabulary at the pinned revision. Without it the statement is false: a
463	Hironaka-type free `ℤ/2`-action on a smooth proper non-projective 3-fold
464	gives a smooth proper equivalence relation satisfying hypotheses (1)–(4)
465	whose quotient étale sheaf is an algebraic space that is not a scheme. In
466	particular there is no global instance of `HasSmoothProperQuotient`; such an
467	instance would assert that every presheaf receiving any natural
468	transformation is representable.
469	
470	`HasSmoothProperQuotient α` is therefore an **explicit use-site hypothesis**:
471	the intended consumer (the FGA assembly, Step 4 of `th:main`) instantiates it
472	for the Abel-map slice `Z ⟶ P^{φ_0}_0`, where `Z` is a quasi-projective open
473	of `Div_{C/k}` and Altman–Kleiman descent genuinely applies. Supplying that
474	instance is part of the `instHasPicScheme` obligation, not a standalone
475	global fact.
476	
477	Blueprint reference: `lem:smooth_proper_quotient` (Kleiman §4 Lem. `lm:qt`). -/
478	
479	/-- Hypothesis class packaging the CONCLUSION of the Altman–Kleiman
480	smooth-proper quotient lemma for a specific étale-sheaf surjection `α`:
481	that the target presheaf is representable.
482	
483	There is deliberately no global instance: an unconditional one would be a
484	false statement (see the section header). The class is supplied at the use
485	site, where the Kleiman `lm:qt` hypotheses — including quasi-projectivity of
486	the representing scheme, which the `smoothProperQuotient` statement below
487	cannot express — actually hold.
488	
489	The class is kept as the blueprint-pinned record of the Altman–Kleiman
490	`lm:qt` interface. A route to `instHasPicScheme` that takes only finite
491	Galois quotients with an orbit-in-affine hypothesis sidesteps the
492	Hironaka-type counterexample above, and so needs neither this class nor
493	`smoothProperQuotient`. -/
494	class HasSmoothProperQuotient {k : Type u} [Field k]
495	    {Z P : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (u + 1)}
496	    (_α : Z ⟶ P) : Prop where
497	  is_representable : P.IsRepresentable
498	
499	/-- **The smooth-proper quotient lemma — Altman–Kleiman descent of an
500	étale-sheaf surjection** (Kleiman §4 Lem. `lm:qt`).
501	
502	Let `Z, P : (Sch/k)^op ⥤ Type (u+1)` be presheaves and `α : Z ⟶ P` a natural
503	transformation with: (1) `Z` representable by `Y`; (2) `R := Z ×_P Z`
504	representable by `R`; (3) the first projection `π : R ⟶ Y` smooth and proper;
505	(4) `α` an étale-local surjection (every `T`-point of `P` lifts along some
506	test morphism). Then, granting the use-site hypothesis
507	`[HasSmoothProperQuotient α]` (which additionally encodes Kleiman's
508	quasi-projectivity of `Y` — see the section header for why it cannot yet be
509	stated internally), `P` is representable.
510	
511	The Lean body extracts the conclusion from the hypothesis class; the
512	mathematical content (Altman–Kleiman effective-equivalence-relation descent
513	+ EGA IV 8.11.5) lives at the use site supplying the instance. -/
514	theorem smoothProperQuotient {k : Type u} [Field k]
515	    {Z P : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (u + 1)}
516	    (α : Z ⟶ P)
517	    (Y : Over (Spec (.of k)))
518	    (_hZ : Z.RepresentableBy Y)
519	    (R : Over (Spec (.of k)))
520	    (_hR : (Limits.pullback α α).RepresentableBy R)
521	    (π : R ⟶ Y)
522	    [Smooth π.left] [IsProper π.left]
523	    (_hα : ∀ ⦃T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ⦄ (p : P.obj T),
524	        ∃ (T' : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ) (e : T ⟶ T') (z : Z.obj T'),
525	          α.app T' z = P.map e p)
526	    [HasSmoothProperQuotient α] :
527	    P.IsRepresentable :=
528	  HasSmoothProperQuotient.is_representable (_α := α)
529	
530	/-! ## §4. The FGA representability theorem
531	
532	Grothendieck's existence theorem for the Picard scheme (Kleiman §4 Thm.
533	`th:main`, specialised via Cor. `cor:algsch` to `S = Spec k`, `X = C`),
534	transported through Kleiman §2 Thm 2.5 to the plain relative functor under
535	the rational-point hypothesis: `picSharp C` is representable by `PicScheme C`.
536	
537	Blueprint reference: `thm:fga_pic_representability`. -/
538	
539	/-- Typeclass asserting that `picSharp C` is representable by `PicScheme C`.
540	
541	It follows from `HasPicScheme` — the representing witness is
542	`Classical.choose`-extracted, so its `choose_spec` is exactly this statement.
543	The class survives to preserve the blueprint-pinned consumer signature of
544	`representable`. -/
545	class PicSharpRepresentable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
546	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
547	    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicScheme C] : Prop where
548	  has_representable : Nonempty ((picSharp C).RepresentableBy (PicScheme C))
549	
550	/-- Existence instance for `PicSharpRepresentable`: `PicScheme C` is
551	`Classical.choose` of the `HasPicScheme` existential, and the first component
552	of `Exists.choose_spec` says precisely that the chosen scheme represents
553	`picSharp C` (the remaining components are local finiteness and
554	separatedness). The FGA content lives upstream in `instHasPicScheme`. -/
555	instance instPicSharpRepresentable {k : Type u} [Field k]
556	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
557	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
558	    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicScheme C] : PicSharpRepresentable C :=
559	  ⟨(HasPicScheme.has_pic_scheme (C := C)).choose_spec.1⟩
560	
561	/-- **FGA representability of the Picard scheme.**
562	
563	Let `k` be a field and `C` a smooth proper geometrically integral curve over
564	`k` (with, through the `HasPicScheme` hypothesis chain, a `k`-rational
565	point). Then the relative Picard functor `Pic^♯_{C/k}` is representable by
566	the Picard scheme `PicScheme C`: there is a natural bijection
567	
568	```
569	(T ⟶ Pic_{C/k}) ≃ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)
570	```
571	
572	for every `k`-scheme `T`. This `RepresentableBy` structure is a comparison
573	against the relative Picard functor itself, so downstream consumers
574	(tangent-space computation at the identity, `Pic⁰` degree theory) can compose
575	with its `homEquiv` to transfer line-bundle data to scheme points. -/
576	noncomputable def representable {k : Type u} [Field k]
577	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
578	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
579	    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicScheme C] [PicSharpRepresentable C] :
580	    (picSharp C).RepresentableBy (PicScheme C) :=
581	  Classical.choice (PicSharpRepresentable.has_representable (C := C))
582	
583	/-! ## §5. The abelian group-scheme structure
584	
585	The Picard scheme `Pic_{C/k}` inherits an abelian group-scheme structure from
586	the tensor product of invertible sheaves on `C ×_k T`: the relative Picard
587	presheaf is group-valued (`PicSharp.relPresheaf`), and a representing object
588	of (the set-valued shadow of) a group-valued presheaf is canonically a group
589	object, by Yoneda transport (`GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy`).
590	
591	Since `picSharp` is by definition `relPresheaf ⋙ forget`, the transport
592	applies directly.
593	
594	Blueprint reference: `thm:pic_is_group_scheme` (Kleiman §2 Def. `df:Pfs` +
595	§4 Def. `df:Psch`). -/
596	
597	/-- The multiplicative (`CommGrpCat`-valued) avatar of the relative Picard
598	presheaf, used to feed `GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy` (whose API is
599	multiplicative). Carrier-level it is the same functor: `Multiplicative` is a
600	type synonym. -/
601	noncomputable def picSharpCommGrp {k : Type u} [Field k]
602	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
603	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :
604	    (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat.{u+1} :=
605	  PicSharp.relPresheaf C ⋙ AddCommGrpCat.toCommGrp
606	
607	/-- The set-valued shadows of `picSharpCommGrp` and `picSharp` agree up to
608	the canonical `Multiplicative.ofAdd` bijection (a natural isomorphism, since
609	`Multiplicative` is carrier-preserving). -/
610	noncomputable def picSharpCommGrpForgetIso {k : Type u} [Field k]
611	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
612	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :
613	    picSharp C ≅ picSharpCommGrp C ⋙ CategoryTheory.forget CommGrpCat.{u+1} :=
614	  NatIso.ofComponents
615	    (fun T => Equiv.toIso (Multiplicative.ofAdd
616	      (α := ((PicSharp.relPresheaf C).obj T : Type (u+1)))))
617	    (fun _ => rfl)
618	
619	/-- **The Picard scheme is a commutative `k`-group scheme** — a canonical
620	`CommGrpObj` structure (i.e. `GrpObj` + `IsCommMonObj`) on `PicScheme C`,
621	obtained by Yoneda transport (`CommGrpObj.ofRepresentableBy`) of the
622	abelian-group structure of the relative Picard presheaf
623	`PicSharp.relPresheaf` along the representability witness `representable C`.
624	Concretely: `[L] + [M] = [L ⊗ M]`, `-[L] = [L⁻¹]`, unit `[O_{C ×_k T}]`,
625	transported through `(T ⟶ Pic_{C/k}) ≃ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)`.
626	
627	Commutativity comes for free from the transport, so this is the full
628	abelian-group-scheme statement of the blueprint
629	(`thm:pic_is_group_scheme`). -/
630	noncomputable instance groupSchemeStructure {k : Type u} [Field k]
631	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
632	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
633	    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicScheme C] :
634	    CommGrpObj (PicScheme C) :=
635	  CommGrpObj.ofRepresentableBy (PicScheme C) (picSharpCommGrp C)

1394	
1395	The disjoint-union structure of `Pic_{C/k}` (a disjoint union of open
1396	quasi-projective `k`-subschemes, indexed by Hilbert polynomial via
1397	`PicScheme.smoothProperQuotient`) stratifies its `T`-points by the leading

10	/-!
11	# FGA representability of the Picard scheme
12	
13	This file states the FGA representability of the relative Picard functor of a
14	smooth proper geometrically integral curve `C/k`, following Kleiman, "The
15	Picard scheme", §2 and §4 (cf. FGA Explained Ch. 9; arXiv:math/0504020).
16	
17	The relative Picard functor is
18	
19	```
20	picSharp C := PicSharp.relPresheaf C ⋙ forget AddCommGrpCat
21	```
22	
23	the set-valued shadow of the `H_T`-coset carrier
24	`T ↦ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)` of `Picard/RelPicFunctor.lean` (Kleiman §2
25	Def. `df:Pfs`; blueprint `def:rel_pic_sharp`). A `RepresentableBy` witness
26	against it is a natural bijection
27	`(T ⟶ Pic_{C/k}) ≃ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)`, which is what the downstream
28	tangent-space computation (`AJC.pic0av`, `Pic0.tangentSpaceIso`) attaches to.
29	
30	## The étale-sheafification route: Kleiman §2 Thm 2.5
31	
32	Kleiman §4 represents the **étale-sheafified** functor `Pic_{(C/k)ét}`.
33	Mathlib at the pinned revision has no étale Grothendieck topology on
34	schemes, so instead of sheafifying we use Kleiman §2 **Thm 2.5**: when
35	`f : X → S` has a **section** and `O_S = f_* O_X` holds universally (true
36	for our proper geometrically integral `C/k`), the comparison maps
37	
38	```
39	Pic_{X/S}(T) → Pic_{(X/S)ét}(T) → Pic_{(X/S)fppf}(T)
40	```
41	
42	are all **bijective**. Hence, under a `k`-rational-point hypothesis
43	(`HasRationalPoint C` below), the *plain* relative functor `picSharp C` is
44	itself representable, and the FGA statement can be made against it directly
45	— no étale topology needed. Without a section the plain functor is not
46	representable in general (it need not even be a Zariski sheaf), which is why
47	representability is asserted only **conditionally on `[HasRationalPoint C]`**:
48	an unconditional statement would be false. For the same reason `picSharp` may
49	not be wired to the *absolute* functor `PicSharp.presheaf`.
50	
51	## Main results
52	
53	* `picSharp` — the relative Picard functor `Pic^♯_{C/k}`.
54	* `divFunctor` — the relative-divisor functor `Scheme.DivFunctor C.hom` of
55	  `Picard/DivFunctorDef.lean` (Kleiman §3 Def. `df:div`, invertible-kernel
56	  quotient encoding).
57	* `PicScheme`, `representable`, `instPicSharpRepresentable` — the representing
58	  scheme and the natural bijection
59	  `(T ⟶ Pic_{C/k}) ≃ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)` it induces.
60	* `instPicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType`, `isSeparated` — `Pic_{C/k}` is locally
61	  of finite type and separated over `k` (Kleiman §4 Thm `th:main`(1): it is a
62	  disjoint union of open quasi-projective `k`-subschemes).
63	* `groupSchemeStructure` — `Pic_{C/k}` is a commutative `k`-group scheme, by
64	  Yoneda transport (`CommGrpObj.ofRepresentableBy`) of the abelian-group
65	  structure of `PicSharp.relPresheaf`.
66	* `abelMapWitness`, `abelMap`, `abelMap_app_mk` — the Abel map
67	  `Div_{C/k} ⟶ Pic^♯_{C/k}`, `[D] ↦ [O(D)] = -[ker q]` (Kleiman §3
68	  Def. `dfn:Abel`), assembled as `abelKernelNatTrans C ≫ picNeg C`.
69	* `smoothProperQuotient` — the Altman–Kleiman quotient lemma (Kleiman §4
70	  Lem. `lm:qt`), relative to the use-site hypothesis class
71	  `HasSmoothProperQuotient`.
72	
73	## Remaining obligations
74	
75	One statement in this file is still `sorry`: `instHasPicScheme`, the existence
76	of a scheme that represents `picSharp C` and is separated and locally of
77	finite type over `k`, given a rational point. Mathematically this is Kleiman
78	§4 Thm `th:main`(1) together with Cor `cor:algsch`, transported through §2
79	Thm 2.5. Everything else here — in particular representability of the chosen
80	scheme, its local finiteness, its separatedness, and its group-scheme
81	structure — is derived from that one existence statement.
82	
83	`smoothProperQuotient` is stated against an explicit hypothesis class rather
84	than proved outright, because the hypothesis list expressible here is weaker
85	than Kleiman §4 Lem. `lm:qt`: it omits quasi-projectivity of the representing
86	scheme `Y`, for which Mathlib has no vocabulary at the pinned revision.
87	Without that hypothesis the statement is false — a Hironaka-type free
88	`ℤ/2`-action on a smooth proper non-projective 3-fold gives a smooth proper
89	equivalence relation whose quotient étale sheaf is an algebraic space that is
90	not a scheme. The class must therefore be supplied at the use site, where
91	quasi-projectivity of the Abel-map slice is available.
92	
93	## References
94	
95	Blueprint: `blueprint/src/chapters/Picard_FGAPicRepresentability.tex`.
96	Kleiman, "The Picard scheme" (arXiv:math/0504020): §2 Thm 2.5
97	(`th:comp` comparison under a section), §3 Def `dfn:Abel` + Thm `th:repDiv`,
98	§4 Thm `th:main` + Cor `cor:algsch` + Lem `lm:qt`.
99	-/

267	/-! ## §2. The Abel map — line-bundle / Quot correspondence
268	
269	The bridge from line bundles on `C ×_k T` to the Quot scheme is the **Abel
270	map**: a relative effective divisor `D ⊆ C ×_k T` over `T` determines a
271	`T`-point of `Div_{C/k}`, and the dual ideal sheaf
272	`O_{C ×_k T}(D) := I_D⁻¹` represents a class in `Pic^♯_{C/k}(T)`.
273	
274	Blueprint reference: `lem:line_bundle_quot_correspondence` (Kleiman §3
275	Def. `dfn:Abel` + Thm. `th:repDiv`). -/
276	
277	/-! ### The Abel map
278	
279	The class `HasAbelMap` carries the map itself (a data field `abel`), so that
280	`abelMap` has the defining property `abelMap_app_mk` below; the instance
281	supplies the explicit natural transformation `abelMapWitness C`.
282	
283	Construction of `abelMapWitness C : Div_{C/k} ⟶ Pic^♯_{C/k}`, `[D] ↦ [O(D)]`:
284	a relative effective divisor family `⟨F, q⟩` on `C ×_k T` has invertible ideal
285	`I_D = ker q`; the Abel map sends its class to
286	`[O(D)] = [I_D⁻¹] = -[I_D]`, the additive inverse (in the group-valued target
287	`Pic^♯_{C/k}(T)`) of the class of the ideal sheaf.  It is assembled as the
288	composite `abelKernelNatTrans C ≫ picNeg C`, where `abelKernelNatTrans` is the
289	substantive `[D] ↦ [I_D]` transformation and `picNeg` is the (natural)
290	negation on the group-valued functor.
291	
292	Naturality of `abelKernelNatTrans` is the mathematical heart: for a test map
293	`g : T' ⟶ T` the base-change square is cartesian (`quotBaseSquare`), and the
294	**kernel–pullback comparison** `g_C^*(ker q) ⟶ ker(g_C^* q)` is an isomorphism
295	under the divisor conditions (`Modules.isIso_pullbackKernelComparison`, whose
296	side hypotheses — epi `q`, quasi-coherent source, finitely-presented `F`,
297	`T`-flat `F`, invertible kernel — are exactly the fields of `DivFamily`), so
298	`ker` commutes with base change and the class `[ker q]` is natural.  Negation
299	is natural because `Pic^♯`'s pullback maps are group homomorphisms.

15	/-!
16	# `Pic⁰_{C/k}` as an abelian variety (A.3.iii–vii)
17	
18	This file is the **iter-193 Pic0AbelianVariety** file-skeleton (NEW lane,
19	blueprint-doctor flagged orphan resolution for the iter-192 plan-phase chapter
20	`Picard_Pic0AbelianVariety.tex`). It packages the strategy phase A.3.iii–vi
21	substrate and the A.3.vii assembly into the load-bearing Route~A statement
22	`Pic⁰_{C/k}` is an abelian variety, the gate of `thm:nonempty_jacobianWitness`
23	for `g(C) ≥ 1` curves.
24	
25	The chapter consumes the abstract identity-component substrate set up in
26	`Picard/IdentityComponent.lean` (`Pic⁰_{C/k}` as a clopen subgroup scheme of
27	finite type, geometrically irreducible, formation commuting with base change)
28	and adds the curve-specific input: the tangent-space isomorphism
29	`T₀ Pic⁰_{C/k} ≅ H¹(C, 𝒪_C)`, the resulting smoothness of dimension `g` at
30	the origin (hence everywhere by translation), properness inherited from the
31	projectivity of `Pic⁰_{C/k}` for `C/k` geometrically normal, and the assembly
32	into an abelian variety in the sense of Milne §I.1.
33	
34	## Status (run 0015, T16 W12-tangent session; previously run 0008 T5)
35	
36	Proved sorry-free in this file: `grpObj` (the `GrpObj (Pic0Scheme C)`
37	structure, via `IdentityComponent.isSubgroupHomomorphism` +
38	`PicScheme.groupSchemeStructure`), `tangentSpaceCotangentDual`,
39	`geometricallyIrreducible` (specialisation of the sibling's
40	`isFiniteTypeGeometricallyIrreducible`, whose QC∧GeomIrred conjuncts were
41	closed in run 0009 — `IdentityComponent.lean`, Kleiman §5 Lem.~`lem:agps`(3)),
42	the `isAbelianVariety` assembly, and the moved
43	`Pic0Scheme.isAbelianVariety` (blueprint pin `thm:pic_zero_is_abelian_variety`).
44	
45	Remaining `sorry` bodies: `finrank_cotangentSpaceDual_eq_finrank_h1Cok` —
46	the wave-5 W12-cocycle reduced core of the Kleiman §5 Thm 5.11 dimension
47	identity: `dim_{κ(e)} Dual(m_e/m_e²) = dim_k Ȟ¹(S, 𝒪_C)` against the concrete
48	two-chart Čech cokernel of any 2-affine cover `S`. The formerly-sorried
49	dimension identity `finrank_cotangentSpace_eq_finrank_hModuleOne` (which
50	`tangentSpaceIso` consumes, via the run-0015
51	`nonempty_cotangentSpaceAddEquiv_of_finrank_eq` reduction of
52	`Picard/Pic0TangentSpace.lean`) is now PROVED from the reduced core by
53	`Subspace.dual_finrank_eq` + the genus lane's cover
54	(`Adelic.exists_affineCoverMVSquare_module_finite_H1Cok`) + the gate-free
55	comparison `AffineCoverMVSquare.hModuleOneEquivH1Cok_curve`. Wave-4
56	W12-finrank closed the **representability leg**
57	(`pointedDualNumberPoints_equiv_relPicKernel`,
58	`cotangentSpaceDual_equiv_relPicKernel` below, set-level both directions) and
59	landed the Mumford `ε ↦ aε` scaling substrate; wave-5 landed the **two-chart
60	Čech unit-cocycle engine** (`DualNumber.truncExpCechKernelAddEquiv`,
61	`Picard/Pic0DualNumberCocycle.lean` §6 — the algebra layer of the cocycle
62	leg, with Mumford-scaling equivariance). The remaining content of the core is
63	the geometric chart-triviality/section-identification substrate plus the
64	`k`-(semi)linearity bookkeeping — and `smooth`, `proper`.
65	
66	The 5 blueprint-pinned declarations are:
67	
68	1. `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Pic0.tangentSpaceIso` (theorem, A.3.iii) — the
69	   canonical isomorphism `T₀ Pic⁰_{C/k} ≅ H¹(C, 𝒪_C)` (Kleiman §5
70	   Thm.~`thm:tgtsp`). Packaged as an `AddEquiv` between the cotangent space
71	   `m_e/m_e²` at a `k`-rational identity-section point `e` and the project's
72	   first-cohomology `k`-module `Scheme.HModule k (Scheme.toModuleKSheaf C) 1`
73	   (from `Genus.lean`). The `k`-module structure on the cotangent space at a
74	   `k`-rational point is supplied as part of the existential bundle.
75	2. `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Pic0.smooth` (theorem, A.3.iv) — `Pic⁰_{C/k}` is
76	   `Smooth` over `k`. Kleiman §5 Cor.~`cor:sm` + Cor.~`cor:ch0`
77	   (characteristic-zero) + Ex.~`ex:jac` (curve case).
78	3. `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Pic0.proper` (theorem, A.3.v) — `Pic⁰_{C/k}` is
79	   `IsProper` over `k`. Kleiman §5 Thm.~`th:qpp&p` (projectivity upgrade for
80	   geometrically normal `C/k`).
81	4. `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Pic0.geometricallyIrreducible` (theorem, A.3.vi)
82	   — `Pic⁰_{C/k}` is `GeometricallyIrreducible` over `k`. Specialisation of
83	   `IdentityComponent.isFiniteTypeGeometricallyIrreducible` (sibling) to
84	   `G = PicScheme C`. Kleiman §5 Prp.~`prp:pic0`.
85	5. `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Pic0.isAbelianVariety` (theorem, A.3.vii) —
86	   `Pic⁰_{C/k}` is an abelian variety: `IsProper ∧ Smooth ∧
87	   GeometricallyIrreducible ∧ Nonempty (GrpObj _)`. Milne §I.1, p.~8
88	   (defining axioms) + Kleiman §5 Rmk.~`rmk:Jac`. Load-bearing A.3.vii gate
89	   of Route~A.
90	
91	## Note on type expressivity
92	
93	Following the project rule "Never weaken the type to dodge the proof", each
94	pinned declaration carries a substantive, non-tautological type:
95	
96	- `tangentSpaceIso C` — existentially quantifies over a `k`-rational
97	  identity-section point `e : Spec k ⟶ (Pic0Scheme C).left` and a `k`-module
98	  structure on the cotangent space `m_e/m_e²` (the `k`-module structure
99	  arising via the `k`-algebra structure on the stalk at a `k`-rational point;
100	  for the file-skeleton this Module instance is bundled as part of the Σ').
101	  Bundles an `AddEquiv` between the cotangent space and the
102	  `H¹(C, 𝒪_C)`-as-`k`-module. The body is iter-194+ work.
103	- `smooth C`, `proper C`, `geometricallyIrreducible C` — genuine `Prop`-valued
104	  statements on the structural morphism `(Pic0Scheme C).hom : Pic⁰_{C/k} ⟶
105	  Spec k`, not tautological.
106	- `isAbelianVariety C` — assembles the conjunction of the four
107	  abelian-variety properties (proper, smooth, geometrically irreducible,
108	  group-object structure); not vacuous because each conjunct is a genuine
109	  property/structure on the (typed-sorry) `Pic0Scheme C`.
110	
111	## Coordination with `Pic0Scheme`
112	
113	The underlying `k`-scheme `Pic⁰_{C/k}` is supplied by
114	`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Pic0Scheme C` from sibling
115	`Picard/IdentityComponent.lean` (`def:pic_zero_subscheme` in the blueprint).
116	We do not redefine the underlying scheme here; the `Pic0` namespace below
117	collects the curve-specific abelian-variety facts about `Pic0Scheme C`.
118	
119	## References
120	
121	Blueprint: `blueprint/src/chapters/Picard_Pic0AbelianVariety.tex`
122	(735 LOC, 5 pins). Sources:
123	- Kleiman, "The Picard scheme", §5, Thm.~`thm:tgtsp` (tangent space),
124	  Cor.~`cor:sm` + Cor.~`cor:ch0` (smoothness), Thm.~`th:qpp&p`
125	  (quasi-projectivity/projectivity), Prp.~`prp:pic0` (irreducibility),
126	  Rmk.~`rmk:Jac` (assembly to abelian scheme); arXiv:math/0504020.
127	- Milne, "Abelian Varieties" (course notes, 2008), §I.1, p.~8
128	  (definition of abelian variety) + Rmk. III.1.4(e) (dimension equals genus).
129	-/

10	/-!
11	# Representability of the Quot scheme (honest statement)
12	
13	The endgame statement of the A.2.b Quot-scheme chapter
14	(`thm:quot_representable`, [Nitsure] §5 "Main Existence Theorems"): for a
15	projective morphism `π : X ⟶ S` over a locally noetherian base, carrying a
16	relatively very ample line bundle `L`, and a coherent sheaf `E`, the Quot
17	functor `Quot^{Φ,L}_{E/X/S}` (`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.QuotFunctor`,
18	`Picard/QuotFunctorDef.lean`) is representable by an `S`-scheme.
19	
20	This file carries the **faithful restatement** settled in inbox `I-0118`:
21	projectivity of `π` with very ample `L` is encoded by
22	`Scheme.Hom.IsProjectiveWith` (`Picard/ProjectiveMorphism.lean` — a closed
23	immersion into `ℙ(Fin (d+1); S)` over `S` with `L ≅ i^* O(1)`).  The
24	statement lives here rather than in `QuotFunctorDef.lean` because the
25	projectivity vocabulary imports that file; this split mirrors
26	`Grassmannian.representable` (`GrassmannianRepresentability.lean`).
27	Everything is at `Scheme.{0}`: `IsProjectiveWith` rests on the Serre twist,
28	hence on the universe-monomorphic descent engine `Scheme.Modules.glue`
29	(`GlueDescent.lean`).
30	
31	The proof is open — the Quot endgame of [Nitsure] §5 (boundedness by
32	Castelnuovo–Mumford regularity, embedding into a relative Grassmannian,
33	flattening stratification, valuative criterion); the theorem below is its
34	single tracked `sorry`.
35	
36	Blueprint: `thm:quot_representable`
37	(`blueprint/src/chapters/Picard_QuotScheme.tex`).
38	Source: [Nitsure] §5 (FGA Explained Ch. 5, arXiv:math/0504020).
39	-/
40	
41	open CategoryTheory Limits
42	
43	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
44	
45	namespace Scheme
46	
47	/-- **Representability of the Quot scheme** (Grothendieck, Altman–Kleiman;
48	`thm:quot_representable`, [Nitsure] §5 "Main Existence Theorems"): let `S`
49	be locally noetherian, `π : X ⟶ S` projective carrying the relatively very
50	ample line bundle `L` (`Scheme.Hom.IsProjectiveWith` — the faithful encoding
51	settled in inbox `I-0118`), `E` a coherent (finitely presented) sheaf on `X`
52	and `Φ ∈ ℚ[λ]`.  Then the Quot functor `Quot^{Φ,L}_{E/X/S}` is representable
53	by an `S`-scheme.  Projectivity supplies finite type
54	(`IsProjectiveWith.locallyOfFiniteType`), so the statement carries no
55	separate `[LocallyOfFiniteType π]` binder.
56	
57	History (inbox `I-0118`): an earlier pin of this theorem hypothesized only
58	`[IsProper π] [LocallyOfFiniteType π]` over arbitrary quasi-coherent `L` and
59	arbitrary `E`.  That signature is *not* the cited theorem and is
60	false-or-open: for merely proper `π` the Quot functor is in general only an
61	algebraic space (Hironaka's smooth proper non-projective 3-fold gives the
62	standard counterexample family).
63	
64	NAMED LEAF (`sorry`): the proof is the [Nitsure] §5 route — boundedness by
65	Castelnuovo–Mumford `m`-regularity, embedding into a relative Grassmannian
66	by pushing forward twists (`Grassmannian.representable`,
67	`GrassmannianRepresentability.lean`), flattening stratification
68	(`AlgebraicGeometry.flatteningStratification`), and the valuative criterion
69	for closedness of the locus — and awaits the Serre-finiteness lane
70	(`sectionGradedModule_fg`, `Picard/SerreFiniteness.lean`, inbox `I-0109`)
71	plus the Castelnuovo–Mumford boundedness input, which stays a
72	blueprint-side target for now. -/
73	theorem QuotScheme {S X : Scheme.{0}} [IsLocallyNoetherian S]
74	    (π : X ⟶ S) (L E : X.Modules) [L.IsQuasicoherent]
75	    (hproj : π.IsProjectiveWith L) (hE : E.IsFinitePresentation)
76	    (Φ : Polynomial ℚ) :
77	    haveI := hproj.locallyOfFiniteType
78	    ∃ (Q : Over S), Nonempty ((QuotFunctor π L E Φ).RepresentableBy Q) := by
79	  sorry
80	
81	end Scheme
82	
83	end AlgebraicGeometry

300	
301	The `dual` route (`Modules.dual (ker q)` as an explicit inverse) is available
302	for the *object-level* invertibility (`dual_isLocallyTrivial`) but is not used
303	here: the group-inverse `-[ker q]` is the canonical `[I_D⁻¹]` and makes
304	naturality rest only on the kernel–pullback comparison, avoiding the
305	not-yet-formalised sheaf-level dual-pullback commutation.
306	
307	Blueprint reference: `lem:line_bundle_quot_correspondence` (Kleiman §3
308	Def. `dfn:Abel`); this instance is the **natural-transformation half** — `Div`
309	representability (Kleiman §3 Thm. `th:repDiv`) is NOT claimed here. -/
310	
311	/-- Well-definedness of the ideal-class assignment `⟨F, q⟩ ↦ [ker q]` on the
312	divisor equivalence relation `DivFamily.Rel`: an equivalence `f : x.F ≅ y.F`
313	with `x.q ≫ f.hom = y.q` gives `ker x.q ≅ ker y.q` (`kernelCompMono` at the
314	iso `f.hom`), hence equal `H_T`-coset classes (`relPicRel_of_iso`). -/
315	private theorem abelKernel_welldef {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
316	    (T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ) {x y : DivFamily C.hom T.unop} (h : x.Rel y) :
317	    Quotient.mk (PicSharp.relPicSetoid C.hom T.unop.hom)
318	        (⟨kernel x.q, x.kerLocallyTrivial⟩ : LineBundle.OnProduct C.hom T.unop.hom) =
319	      Quotient.mk (PicSharp.relPicSetoid C.hom T.unop.hom)
320	        (⟨kernel y.q, y.kerLocallyTrivial⟩ : LineBundle.OnProduct C.hom T.unop.hom) := by
321	  obtain ⟨f, hf⟩ := h
322	  exact Quotient.sound (PicSharp.relPicRel_of_iso
323	    ⟨(kernelCompMono x.q f.hom).symm ≪≫ Limits.kernelIsoOfEq hf⟩)
324	
325	/-- **Kernel commutes with base change for a divisor family** (the mathematical
326	heart of Abel-map naturality).  For a test map `g : T ⟶ T'` and a divisor family
327	`x` over `T`, the ideal of the pulled-back family is the pullback of the ideal:
328	`ker((g_C^* x).q) ≅ g_C^*(ker x.q)`.  Proof: `(pullbackAlong g.unop x).q` is
329	`triangleIso.inv ≫ g_C^*(x.q)`, so its kernel agrees with `ker(g_C^* x.q)`
330	(`kernelIsIsoComp`, precomposition by the iso `triangleIso.inv`); the
331	**kernel–pullback comparison** `g_C^*(ker q) ⟶ ker(g_C^* q)` is an isomorphism
332	under the divisor conditions (`Modules.isIso_pullbackKernelComparison`, whose
333	side hypotheses are exactly the `DivFamily` fields `epi`, quasi-coherent source,
334	`isFinitePresentation`, `flat`, `kerLocallyTrivial` over the cartesian
335	`quotBaseSquare`). -/
336	private noncomputable def abelKernelBaseChangeIso {k : Type u} [Field k]
337	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
338	    {T T' : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ} (g : T ⟶ T') (x : DivFamily C.hom T.unop) :
339	    kernel ((DivFamily.pullbackAlong g.unop x).q) ≅
340	      (Scheme.Modules.pullback (quotBaseMap C.hom g.unop)).obj (kernel x.q) := by
341	  haveI hiso : IsIso (Modules.pullbackKernelComparison (quotBaseMap C.hom g.unop) x.q) :=
342	    Modules.isIso_pullbackKernelComparison (quotBaseSquare C.hom g.unop) x.q x.epi
343	      (pullback_isQuasicoherent_hom (pullback.fst C.hom T.unop.hom)
344	        (SheafOfModules.unit C.left.ringCatSheaf) inferInstance)
345	      x.isFinitePresentation x.flat x.kerLocallyTrivial
346	  exact kernelIsIsoComp
347	      (pullbackTriangleIso (quotBaseMap_fst C.hom g.unop)
348	        (SheafOfModules.unit C.left.ringCatSheaf)).inv
349	      ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (quotBaseMap C.hom g.unop)).map x.q) ≪≫
350	    (asIso (Modules.pullbackKernelComparison (quotBaseMap C.hom g.unop) x.q)).symm
351	
352	/-- **The ideal-class transformation** `[D] ↦ [I_D] = [ker q]`
353	(`Div_{C/k} ⟶ Pic^♯_{C/k}`), the additive negative of the Abel map.  On
354	objects it is `⟦⟨F, q⟩⟧ ↦ ⟦ker q⟧`; naturality is the invertible
355	kernel–pullback comparison over the cartesian base-change square
356	(`abelKernelBaseChangeIso`, fed by the `DivFamily` fields).  Well-definedness on
357	`DivFamily.Rel` is `abelKernel_welldef`. -/
358	noncomputable def abelKernelNatTrans {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
359	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :
360	    divFunctor C ⟶ picSharp C where
361	  app T := TypeCat.ofHom (Quotient.lift
362	    (fun x : DivFamily C.hom T.unop =>
363	      Quotient.mk (PicSharp.relPicSetoid C.hom T.unop.hom)
364	        (⟨kernel x.q, x.kerLocallyTrivial⟩ : LineBundle.OnProduct C.hom T.unop.hom))
365	    (fun _ _ h => abelKernel_welldef C T h))
366	  naturality {T T'} g := by
367	    ext a
368	    induction a using Quotient.ind with | _ x => ?_
369	    apply Quotient.sound
370	    apply PicSharp.relPicRel_of_iso
371	    exact ⟨abelKernelBaseChangeIso C g x⟩
372	
373	/-- **Negation on the group-valued relative Picard presheaf**
374	`PicSharp.relPresheaf C ⟶ PicSharp.relPresheaf C`.  Pointwise it is the group
375	homomorphism `a ↦ -a` (`-AddMonoidHom.id`, valid since `Pic^♯_{C/k}(T)` is
376	abelian); naturality is `map_neg` of the group-homomorphism pullback maps of
377	`Pic^♯` (`PicSharp.relFunctorial`).  Building the negation at the
378	`AddCommGrpCat`-valued level (rather than on the forgotten set-valued
379	`picSharp`) keeps the group structure directly available — the forget-composite
380	`(picSharp C).obj T` does not expose its `AddGroup` to instance search. -/
381	noncomputable def relPresheafNeg {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
382	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :
383	    PicSharp.relPresheaf C ⟶ PicSharp.relPresheaf C where
384	  app T := AddCommGrpCat.ofHom (-AddMonoidHom.id _)
385	  naturality {T T'} g := by
386	    ext a
387	    exact (map_neg (PicSharp.relFunctorial C.hom T.unop.hom T'.unop.hom
388	      g.unop.left (Over.w g.unop).symm) a).symm
389	
390	/-- **Negation on the relative Picard functor**, as a natural transformation
391	`Pic^♯_{C/k} ⟶ Pic^♯_{C/k}`.  Pointwise it is `a ↦ -a` in the group
392	`Pic^♯_{C/k}(T)`; it is the set-valued shadow (`whiskerRight … (forget _)`) of
393	the group-presheaf negation `relPresheafNeg`, so its naturality is inherited
394	for free. -/
395	noncomputable def picNeg {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
396	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :
397	    picSharp C ⟶ picSharp C :=
398	  Functor.whiskerRight (relPresheafNeg C) (CategoryTheory.forget AddCommGrpCat.{u+1})
399	
400	/-- **The Abel map witness** `A_{C/k} : Div_{C/k} ⟶ Pic^♯_{C/k}`,
401	`[D] ↦ [O(D)] = [I_D⁻¹] = -[ker q]`, the substantive natural transformation
402	underlying the line-bundle / Quot correspondence (Kleiman §3 Def. `dfn:Abel`).
403	Assembled as `abelKernelNatTrans C ≫ picNeg C`. -/
404	noncomputable def abelMapWitness {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
405	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :
406	    divFunctor C ⟶ picSharp C :=
407	  abelKernelNatTrans C ≫ picNeg C
408	
409	/-- Class **carrying the Abel map** `Div_{C/k} ⟶ Pic^♯_{C/k}`.  It is a
410	data-carrying class with field `abel`, so `abelMap := HasAbelMap.abel`
411	inherits the concrete construction and the defining property
412	`abelMap_app_mk`.  The instance `instHasAbelMap` supplies the witness
413	`abelMapWitness C`. -/
414	class HasAbelMap {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
415	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
416	    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] where
417	  /-- The Abel map itself (data). -/
418	  abel : divFunctor C ⟶ picSharp C
419	
420	/-- The **Abel map** `A_{C/k} : Div_{C/k} ⟶ Pic^♯_{C/k}`, sending a relative
421	effective Cartier divisor `D ⊆ C ×_k T` over `T` to its associated invertible
422	sheaf `[O_{C ×_k T}(D)] = [I_D⁻¹]`.
423	
424	It is the map carried by `HasAbelMap`; the instance `instHasAbelMap` fixes it
425	to `abelMapWitness C`, and its defining property is `abelMap_app_mk`. -/
426	noncomputable def abelMap {k : Type u} [Field k]
427	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
428	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
429	    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasAbelMap C] :
430	    divFunctor C ⟶ picSharp C :=
431	  HasAbelMap.abel
432	
433	/-- Existence instance for `HasAbelMap`: the Abel map `abelMapWitness C`
434	witnesses the carrier. -/
435	noncomputable instance instHasAbelMap {k : Type u} [Field k]
436	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
437	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
438	    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] : HasAbelMap C :=
439	  ⟨abelMapWitness C⟩

456	surjection `α : Z ⟶ P` of étale sheaves with `R := Z ×_P Z` representable,
457	`Z` representable **by a quasi-projective scheme**, and the first projection
458	`R ⟶ Z` smooth and proper, the quotient `P` is representable.

461	`lm:qt`: it lacks **quasi-projectivity of `Y`**, for which Mathlib has no
462	vocabulary at the pinned revision. Without it the statement is false: a
463	Hironaka-type free `ℤ/2`-action on a smooth proper non-projective 3-fold
464	gives a smooth proper equivalence relation satisfying hypotheses (1)–(4)
465	whose quotient étale sheaf is an algebraic space that is not a scheme. In
466	particular there is no global instance of `HasSmoothProperQuotient`; such an
467	instance would assert that every presheaf receiving any natural

474	instance is part of the `instHasPicScheme` obligation, not a standalone

500	étale-sheaf surjection** (Kleiman §4 Lem. `lm:qt`).

502	Let `Z, P : (Sch/k)^op ⥤ Type (u+1)` be presheaves and `α : Z ⟶ P` a natural
503	transformation with: (1) `Z` representable by `Y`; (2) `R := Z ×_P Z`
504	representable by `R`; (3) the first projection `π : R ⟶ Y` smooth and proper;
505	(4) `α` an étale-local surjection (every `T`-point of `P` lifts along some
506	test morphism). Then, granting the use-site hypothesis
507	`[HasSmoothProperQuotient α]` (which additionally encodes Kleiman's
508	quasi-projectivity of `Y` — see the section header for why it cannot yet be

520	    (_hR : (Limits.pullback α α).RepresentableBy R)
521	    (π : R ⟶ Y)
522	    [Smooth π.left] [IsProper π.left]

530	/-! ## §4. The FGA representability theorem
531	
532	Grothendieck's existence theorem for the Picard scheme (Kleiman §4 Thm.
533	`th:main`, specialised via Cor. `cor:algsch` to `S = Spec k`, `X = C`),
534	transported through Kleiman §2 Thm 2.5 to the plain relative functor under
535	the rational-point hypothesis: `picSharp C` is representable by `PicScheme C`.
536	
537	Blueprint reference: `thm:fga_pic_representability`. -/
538	
539	/-- Typeclass asserting that `picSharp C` is representable by `PicScheme C`.
540	
541	It follows from `HasPicScheme` — the representing witness is
542	`Classical.choose`-extracted, so its `choose_spec` is exactly this statement.
543	The class survives to preserve the blueprint-pinned consumer signature of
544	`representable`. -/
545	class PicSharpRepresentable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
546	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
547	    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicScheme C] : Prop where
548	  has_representable : Nonempty ((picSharp C).RepresentableBy (PicScheme C))
549	
550	/-- Existence instance for `PicSharpRepresentable`: `PicScheme C` is
551	`Classical.choose` of the `HasPicScheme` existential, and the first component
552	of `Exists.choose_spec` says precisely that the chosen scheme represents
553	`picSharp C` (the remaining components are local finiteness and
554	separatedness). The FGA content lives upstream in `instHasPicScheme`. -/
555	instance instPicSharpRepresentable {k : Type u} [Field k]
556	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
557	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
558	    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicScheme C] : PicSharpRepresentable C :=
559	  ⟨(HasPicScheme.has_pic_scheme (C := C)).choose_spec.1⟩

561	/-- **FGA representability of the Picard scheme.**
562	
563	Let `k` be a field and `C` a smooth proper geometrically integral curve over
564	`k` (with, through the `HasPicScheme` hypothesis chain, a `k`-rational
565	point). Then the relative Picard functor `Pic^♯_{C/k}` is representable by
566	the Picard scheme `PicScheme C`: there is a natural bijection
567	
568	```
569	(T ⟶ Pic_{C/k}) ≃ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)
570	```
571	
572	for every `k`-scheme `T`. This `RepresentableBy` structure is a comparison
573	against the relative Picard functor itself, so downstream consumers
574	(tangent-space computation at the identity, `Pic⁰` degree theory) can compose
575	with its `homEquiv` to transfer line-bundle data to scheme points. -/

580	    (picSharp C).RepresentableBy (PicScheme C) :=

583	/-! ## §5. The abelian group-scheme structure
584	
585	The Picard scheme `Pic_{C/k}` inherits an abelian group-scheme structure from
586	the tensor product of invertible sheaves on `C ×_k T`: the relative Picard
587	presheaf is group-valued (`PicSharp.relPresheaf`), and a representing object
588	of (the set-valued shadow of) a group-valued presheaf is canonically a group
589	object, by Yoneda transport (`GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy`).
590	
591	Since `picSharp` is by definition `relPresheaf ⋙ forget`, the transport
592	applies directly.
593	
594	Blueprint reference: `thm:pic_is_group_scheme` (Kleiman §2 Def. `df:Pfs` +
595	§4 Def. `df:Psch`). -/

597	/-- The multiplicative (`CommGrpCat`-valued) avatar of the relative Picard
598	presheaf, used to feed `GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy` (whose API is

601	noncomputable def picSharpCommGrp {k : Type u} [Field k]
602	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
603	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :
604	    (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat.{u+1} :=
605	  PicSharp.relPresheaf C ⋙ AddCommGrpCat.toCommGrp

611	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))

613	    picSharp C ≅ picSharpCommGrp C ⋙ CategoryTheory.forget CommGrpCat.{u+1} :=

615	    (fun T => Equiv.toIso (Multiplicative.ofAdd

619	/-- **The Picard scheme is a commutative `k`-group scheme** — a canonical
620	`CommGrpObj` structure (i.e. `GrpObj` + `IsCommMonObj`) on `PicScheme C`,

628	abelian-group-scheme statement of the blueprint
629	(`thm:pic_is_group_scheme`). -/
630	noncomputable instance groupSchemeStructure {k : Type u} [Field k]
631	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
632	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
633	    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicScheme C] :
634	    CommGrpObj (PicScheme C) :=
635	  CommGrpObj.ofRepresentableBy (PicScheme C) (picSharpCommGrp C)

855	component `Pic⁰_{C/k}` is an abelian variety over `k`: the underlying

import Mathlib
import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.HilbertPolynomial
import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.LineBundlePullback
import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.FlatteningStratification
import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.GlueDescent

/-!
# B3 — the rigid pushforward engine: statement layer and ℙ¹ reduction skeleton

This file pins milestone **B3** of the Picard-representability campaign
(`informal/pic-representability-campaign.md`), the engine
`pushforward_locallyFree_of_h1_vanishing`: for the constant curve
`C_A = C ×_k Spec A` over a finitely generated `k`-algebra `A` and an
invertible sheaf `L` on `C_A` with `h¹(C_t, L_t) = 0` at **every scheme
point** `t : Spec A`, the pushforward `q_* L` along `q : C_A ⟶ Spec A` is
locally free with fibre rank `h⁰(C_t, L_t) (= χ(L_t))`, and its formation
commutes with **arbitrary** ring maps `A → A'`.

Sources: Mumford, *Abelian Varieties*, II §5 (the two-term finite free
complex and "cohomology and base change"); EGA III 7.9.9; Hartshorne III
12.11; Kleiman, *The Picard scheme* (FGA Explained), §5 — B3 is the engine
behind Kleiman's flattening/openness arguments in the curve case.

## Statement audit (campaign checklist item 1 — BLOCKING; verdicts recorded here)

* **Quantifier — `h¹ = 0` at ALL scheme points** (`RigidPushforwardLocallyFree`,
  `RigidPushforwardBaseChange`): the hypothesis `∀ t : Spec A,
  q.FiberH1Vanishing L t` ranges over *all* points of the underlying space of
  `Spec A` (all primes), not only closed points.  For general noetherian `A`
  (noetherian ≠ Jacobson: e.g. a DVR, whose generic point is contained in no
  closed point's closure) the closed-point form is strictly weaker and the
  engine's conclusion FAILS if the hypothesis is checked at closed points
  only.  A finitely generated `k`-algebra *is* Jacobson, so on the pinned
  base the two forms happen to agree — but (i) the reduction uses h¹ upper
  semicontinuity, an engine we refuse to smuggle into the *statement*, and
  (ii) milestone B2 extends every consumer along filtered colimits and
  localizations, where the base is merely noetherian and Jacobson genuinely
  fails.  All campaign consumers (J1/J3 `h⁰ ≡ 1`, B4–B6) supply the
  hypothesis at all scheme points anyway.  VERDICT: pin at all scheme points.
* **Base change along ARBITRARY `A → A'` in the statement**
  (`RigidPushforwardBaseChange`): quantified over every commutative ring
  `A' : Type u` and every ring hom `φ : A →+* A'` — no finiteness, no
  flatness, no noetherian hypothesis on `A'`.  The comparison morphism is
  the canonical `pushforwardBaseChangeMap` (Stacks 02N4-style mate) of the
  *defining pullback square* of `q` along `Spec φ`, so the statement is
  well-formed with zero transport: the base-changed family is
  `pullback q (Spec.map φ)` — canonically (but not definitionally) isomorphic
  to `C ×_k Spec A'`; the comparison iso is postponed to the consumer layer
  (B2), keeping the pin transport-free.  VERDICT: arbitrary `A'`, arbitrary
  `φ`, canonical square, comparison map in the statement.
* **Two-step pin**: step 1 = rank-`χ` local freeness
  (`RigidPushforwardLocallyFree`) + base change
  (`RigidPushforwardBaseChange`); step 2 = the rank-one corollary
  (`pushforward_isLocallyTrivial_of_h1_vanishing`, proved from the gate).
  VERDICT: pinned as two separate `Prop`s consumed by one gate.
* **Rank = `χ(L_t)`** : under `h¹(L_t) = 0` we have `χ(L_t) = h⁰(L_t)`, and
  `h⁰` *is* expressible today (`Scheme.Hom.fiberH0`, the `κ(t)`-dimension of
  `Γ(C_t, L_t)`, matching `Scheme.hilbertFunction`'s convention), while the
  `χ`-ledger is milestone P3.  The rank is therefore pinned as
  `q.fiberH0 L t`; **P2/P3-interface TODO**: once the P2 cohomology kit and
  the P3 `χ`-ledger land, add the (definitionally compatible) reformulation
  `rank = χ(L_t) = deg L_t + 1 - g`.
* **Fibrewise `h¹` vocabulary** (P2 does not exist yet): the hypothesis is
  pinned in the weakest honest form the adelic lane can already express —
  existence of a 2-affine Čech cover (`AffineCoverMVSquare`, the lane's
  carrier) of the scheme-theoretic fibre on which the degree-1 Čech
  cokernel of `L_t` vanishes, i.e. the difference-of-restrictions map is
  surjective (`Scheme.Hom.FiberH1Vanishing`; carrier form
  `AffineCoverMVSquare.moduleH1Cok`, mirroring
  `AffineCoverMVSquare.H1Cok` of `RiemannRoch/Adelic/Cokernel.lean`).  On a
  separated scheme with an affine 2-cover, this Čech `H¹` computes sheaf
  `H¹` for quasi-coherent modules (Mayer–Vietoris/Leray; in-lane precedent
  `hModuleOne_linearEquiv_cechCohomology`), and any two such covers agree —
  cover-independence is exactly the **P2-interface TODO**, to be discharged
  Čech-to-Čech.  The ∃-form is chosen because it is *implied* by every
  future kit form, so the gate only gets easier to discharge.
* **The rank-one corollary's `DivFamily` leg** (Kleiman §5; campaign J2):
  `h⁰ ≡ 1, h¹ ≡ 0 ⟹ q_*L` invertible is pinned and proved from the gate
  below.  The continuation — the counit section `q^*q_*L ⟶ L` is fibrewise
  nonzero, hence a regular section on the integral fibres, hence cuts a
  canonical `DivFamily` — needs the counit/adjunction vocabulary on the
  `Div` side and the geometric integrality of fibres; it is recorded as the
  **J2-interface TODO** and deliberately NOT pinned here (its natural home
  is the J2 session, where the target `DivFamily` shape is fixed).

## Gate

`HasRigidPushforward C` is the campaign gate (`HasPicScheme` pattern): a
`Prop` class with **no instances anywhere**, carrying the two statement
`Prop`s quantified over all finitely generated `k`-algebras.  It is
discharged by the full B3 session (Mumford two-term complex route) and
deleted on discharge.  Everything else in this file is *proved*: the
extraction theorems, the rank-one corollary, and the ℙ¹ reduction skeleton
(the base-changed finite map `C_A ⟶ ℙ¹_A`, the pushforward factorization
`q_* = p_* ∘ π_*`, and the reduction of B3-for-`C_A` to a ℙ¹ engine plus a
named finite-pushforward transfer package).
-/

/-!
# B3 transfer package — discharging the named hypotheses of the ℙ¹ reduction

`Picard/RigidPushforward.lean` reduces B3 local freeness for the constant
curve `C_A` to the ℙ¹ engine plus a *finite-pushforward transfer package*
along the finite map `π_A : C_A ⟶ ℙ¹_A` (`rigidPushforwardLocallyFree_of_p1`,
hypotheses `hfp`/`hflat`/`hH1`/`hH0`).  This file discharges the first two
transfer hypotheses:

* **`hfp` (Stacks 01XZ/087T flavour)** —
  `pushforward_finiteMapToP1BaseChange_isFinitePresentation`: the finite
  pushforward `(π_A)_* L` of an invertible module is finitely presented.
  The engine behind it is the general noetherian coherence criterion
  `Scheme.Modules.isFinitePresentation_of_finite_sections`: a quasi-coherent
  module on a locally noetherian scheme whose section modules over affine
  opens are finite is finitely presented.  The pushforward is quasi-coherent
  by Stacks 01XJ (`pushforward_isQuasicoherent`, proved in
  `Picard/QuotScheme.lean`), its sections over an affine `V` are
  `Γ(L, π_A⁻¹ V)` *definitionally*, and these are module-finite over
  `Γ(ℙ¹_A, V)` by composing the module-finiteness of the finite morphism
  `π_A` (Stacks 01WG) with the finiteness of the sections of the finitely
  presented `L` on the affine `π_A⁻¹ V` (Stacks 01PC,
  `finite_sections_preimage_of_isAffineHom`).  `A` is a finitely generated
  `k`-algebra, hence noetherian (Hilbert basis), hence `ℙ¹_A` is locally
  noetherian and finite section modules are finitely presented.

* **`hflat` (mixed-base flat stability)** —
  `pushforward_finiteMapToP1BaseChange_coherentSheafFlat`: `(π_A)_* L`
  stays `CoherentSheafFlat` over `Spec A`.  Since
  `Γ((π_A)_* L, V) = Γ(L, π_A⁻¹ V)` definitionally and
  `q = π_A ≫ p` (`finiteMapToP1BaseChange_snd`), the statement reduces to
  `CoherentSheafFlat q L` for the invertible `L` on the `A`-flat family
  `q : C_A ⟶ Spec A` (`coherentSheafFlat_pushforward_of_isAffineHom`).
  The latter is `coherentSheafFlat_of_isLocallyTrivial_of_flat`: on a
  trivialising affine chart `W` the section module `Γ(L, W)` is an
  invertible (hence flat) `Γ(C_A, W)`-module
  (`isInvertible_of_restrict_iso`), `Γ(C_A, W)` is flat over `A` because
  `q` is a flat morphism (base change of `C ⟶ Spec k`, and everything over
  the one-point integral `Spec k` is flat), and chart flatness globalises
  to all affine pairs by the affine-locality engine
  `flat_section_of_affine_cover` (`Picard/GenericFlatnessGeometric.lean`).

* **transfer item (c) — the fibre-compatibility isomorphism and `hH0`**
  (§6–§7): the general Stacks 02KG (`i = 0`) engine for **affine**
  morphisms and **arbitrary** (non-flat) base change
  (`isIso_pushforwardBaseChangeMap_of_isPullback`), its fibre specialization
  `fiberPushforwardCompatIso : (p.fiberι t)^* ((π_A)_* L) ≅ (π_t)_* (L_t)`,
  the verbatim `hH0` discharge
  (`pushforward_finiteMapToP1BaseChange_fiberH0`), and the `hH1` transfer
  reduced to Čech cover-independence of `Ȟ¹`-vanishing on the fibre curve
  (`fiberH1Vanishing_pushforward_finiteMapToP1BaseChange_of_coverIndependence`).

* **`hH1`** — the cover-independence obligation `hindep` is
  discharged by the QC-vanishing keystone
  (`Cohomology/StructureSheafModuleK/QuasicoherentDegreeOneVanishing.lean`:
  degree-1 affine vanishing for quasi-coherent modules + the Mayer–Vietoris
  `(0,1)`-slice on every 2-affine cover), giving the verbatim pinned `hH1`
  (`pushforward_finiteMapToP1BaseChange_fiberH1`).  All four transfer
  hypotheses being discharged, B3 local freeness for `C_A` follows from the
  ℙ¹ engine alone (`rigidPushforwardLocallyFree_of_p1Engine`).

No pinned statement is touched: this file only *produces* the named
hypotheses consumed by `rigidPushforwardLocallyFree_of_p1`.

Sources: Stacks 01XJ (pushforward quasi-coherence), 01XZ/087T (finite
pushforward of coherent is coherent), 01PC (finite sections on affines),
01WG (finite morphisms are module-finite on affines), 00HB/00HT (flatness
is affine-local), 02KG (cohomology and base change, `i = 0`); Nitsure §4;
Mumford AV II §5.
-/
